notes.assessment: Muslim 1728 matches Abu Said al-Khudri’s travel report, spare mounts and provisions, and the conclusion about surplus property. The final Japanese rights-against-others phrase merits a conservative semantic correction; see finding REF-47.

findings.original_ja: 私たちはまるで自分たちが所有する剰余物において、他人に対するいかなる権利も有していないかのように感じたものです。
findings.arabic_evidence_excerpt: لاَ حَقَّ لأَحَدٍ مِنَّا فِي فَضْلٍ
findings.assessment: The primary clause concerns any one of the group having a right in surplus property. The Japanese addition 他人に対する shifts the relation toward rights against other people. A literal conservative revision can remove that added relation without asserting a new legal rule.
findings.suggested_editorial_ja: 私たちは、自分たちの誰にも余分な財に対する権利はないと考えるほどでした。
findings.treatment: Use only in an explicitly labeled editorial correction; preserve the original Japanese separately. The proposal is AI-generated editorial Japanese, not a quotation from an existing Japanese edition.

findings.original_ja: 静寂が訪れ、慈悲に包まれ、またアッラーが天使たちのもとで彼らを褒め称えられないことはない
findings.assessment: The cited Arabic includes the angels surrounding the group between mercy and divine mention. This clause is absent from the selected Japanese passage. The book begins with 中略, so deliberate abridgment cannot be ruled out; do not call this an OCR omission or claim authorial intent.

findings.treatment: If producing a fuller corrected editorial text, insert 天使たちに囲まれ、 and label it as a clause restored from Muslim 2699a. Retain the initial source abridgment marker and original wording separately.
